recent_posts.title: AI Is Changing Engineering Teams — Why Psychological Safety Matters More Than Ever
recent_posts.summary: AI adoption is creating a hidden crisis in engineering teams: the erosion of psychological safety. Engineers are being discouraged from questioning AI decisions, overwhelmed by the pace of change, and even senior engineers are struggling to keep up. The post outlines four stages of psychological safety (inclusion, learner, contributor, challenger) and argues that 'challenger safety' is most at risk in the AI era. Leaders are advised to foster growth mindsets, create space for experimentation, reward vulnerability over false certainty, and balance innovation with guardrails. Core engineering skills remain essential and are amplified, not replaced, by AI.

recent_posts.title: Why North Star metrics matter more as AI speeds up software development
recent_posts.summary: AI is dramatically accelerating software development, enabling teams to prototype in hours and ship experiments faster than ever. But this speed amplifies the risk of building the wrong things. The North Star framework — defining a measurable outcome tied to real customer value — becomes more critical as development velocity increases. Key themes include the distinction between leading and lagging metrics, the continued importance of observability, the evolution of engineers into systems thinkers responsible for full product outcomes, and the shift of the real bottleneck from building to decision-making. As AI reduces execution costs, strategic clarity and strong product leadership become the true competitive differentiators.

recent_posts.title: AI: Commodity or Differentiator?
recent_posts.summary: AI has become a platform shift similar to AWS, forcing organizations to decide whether to build or consume AI capabilities. Most should consume AI as infrastructure and differentiate through domain knowledge, customer insight, and workflow integration rather than building foundation models. Key risks include unclear blast radius for agentic AI, misidentifying commodity versus differentiator capabilities, and attempting to replace critical systems with AI-generated code without proper governance. Success requires codifying organizational context, tightening feedback loops, and applying strategic discipline before scaling AI adoption.

recent_posts.title: Six myths about AI's impact on software engineering
recent_posts.summary: Six common misconceptions about AI's impact on software engineering are debunked: the profession isn't dying, core engineering skills remain valuable, AI quality is rapidly improving, models don't truly understand problems, AI adoption should be thoughtful not forced, and demand for skilled engineers will likely increase. The real shift is that AI amplifies the importance of problem-solving, systems thinking, and engineering judgment while automating routine tasks. Success requires applying clarity, constraints, and discipline to more powerful tools rather than chasing hype.

recent_posts.title: Strategic cloud decisions for CTOs
recent_posts.summary: CTOs face critical decisions in cloud strategy, from platform selection to compliance and sustainability. Success requires balancing single-provider depth against multi-cloud flexibility, establishing clear principles and guardrails for teams, and avoiding custom-built solutions in favor of industry standards. Modern CTOs must enable continuous evolution with the right building blocks, navigate complex regulations through shared responsibility models, and treat carbon impact as a key performance indicator alongside traditional metrics.

recent_posts.title: Five Years On: What Writing The Value Flywheel Effect Taught Us About Software, Scale, and Letting Go
recent_posts.summary: Reflecting on five years since writing The Value Flywheel Effect, the authors share lessons about software delivery and organizational change. Writing the book was a refactoring exercise requiring letting go of ownership as ideas were challenged and reshaped. Key insights include: clarity often emerges through delivery rather than upfront planning, AI has amplified the value of codified thinking and clear architectural principles, and the divide between business and technical strategy has blurred. The core lesson is that achieving impact at scale requires creating systems where standards survive without individual ownership, while the fundamental questions about speed, risk management, and long-term value remain unchanged.

recent_posts.title: How the BBC Scales Serverless: A Case Study in Long-Term Value and Problem Prevention
recent_posts.summary: BBC News successfully adopted a serverless-first architecture to handle massive global traffic spikes (up to 2.5 million page views per minute) with a relatively small engineering team. The approach enabled continuous delivery every 20 minutes, improved site performance noticeably, and shifted focus from infrastructure maintenance to feature development. By embracing managed services and architectural constraints, the BBC achieved world-class scale while preventing operational problems and reducing complexity. The case demonstrates how serverless can work for large public-sector organizations with strict uptime requirements, not just startups.

recent_posts.title: Mapping the Emerging Value: Moving Beyond Operations to Strategic Advantage
recent_posts.summary: Explores how engineering leaders can use Wardley Mapping to identify and capture strategic opportunities beyond day-to-day operations. Discusses three organizational pipelines (mindset, purpose, cloud strategy) and three value chains (run, grow, transform) that enable teams to sense emerging market opportunities. Covers strategic gameplay patterns like market enablement, fast follower strategies, and weak signal detection. Emphasizes that pursuing emerging value requires stable systems, clear missions, product-centered teams, and psychological safety as foundational capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Why Organisations Struggle to Create Space for Innovation
recent_posts.summary: Organizations often misapply lean manufacturing principles to innovation work, killing creativity before it starts. The Innovate-Leverage-Commoditise cycle from Wardley Mapping provides a framework for understanding when to explore versus optimize. Domain-driven design helps align teams around business capabilities rather than features. Observability enables the feedback loops necessary for innovation. Well-architected, sustainable systems create the space for innovation by reducing cognitive load and firefighting. Proactive leadership requires situational awareness and strategic preparation rather than reactive problem-solving.

recent_posts.title: Building a Problem Prevention Culture with AWS Well-Architected
recent_posts.summary: Explores how to shift engineering culture from reactive firefighting to proactive problem prevention using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. Introduces SCORP (Security, Cost, Operational Resilience, Reliability, Performance), a lightweight process for continuous quality assessment through short team sessions and dashboards. Emphasizes psychological safety, peer learning, and treating prevention as a strategic capability that enables sustainable velocity and innovation.
